• Mechanism: Selective inhibitor of Janus kinases (primarily JAK3 and JAK1).
• Effect: Interrupts the JAK-STAT signaling pathway, blocking transcription of genes for lymphocyte proliferation.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 670 (Book Page): [Tofacitinib is a targeted synthetic small molecule (tsDMARD) that selectively inhibits all members of the Janus kinase (JAK) family... interrupting the JAK-STAT signaling pathway.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: What is the first-line conventional synthetic DMARD used in the majority of RA patients?
back:
• Methotrexate: Used in 50–70% of patients.
• Primary mechanism: Increases extracellular adenosine, a potent inhibitor of inflammation.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 665 (Book Page): [Methotrexate, a synthetic nonbiologic antimetabolite, is the first-line csDMARD for treating RA and is used in 50–70% of patients.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: List three legacy biologic TNF-alpha blocking agents used for Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back:
1. Adalimumab (Fully human IgG1 antibody)
2. Infliximab (Chimeric IgG1 antibody)
3. Etanercept (Recombinant fusion protein/p75 receptor moiety)
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 667 (Book Page)-669: [Adalimumab is a fully human IgG1 anti-TNF monoclonal antibody... Infliximab is a chimeric... IgG1 monoclonal antibody... Etanercept is a recombinant fusion protein.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Explain the rationale for Prednisone 'chronotherapy' in RA patients regarding morning stiffness.
back:
• Timing: 9–10 PM administration.
• Rationale: Releases a pulse of drug at 2–4 AM to suppress the early morning surge of proinflammatory cytokines.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 672 (Book Page): [Taking the drug at 9–10 pm results in a small pulse of prednisone at 2–4 am, decreasing the circadian inflammatory cytokines.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Identify the biologic agent that inhibits Interleukin-6 (IL-6) signaling.
back:
• Tocilizumab: Humanized antibody.
• Mechanism: Binds to both soluble and membrane-bound IL-6 receptors to block proinflammatory signaling.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 667 (Book Page): [Tocilizumab, a newer biologic humanized antibody, binds to soluble and membrane-bound IL-6 receptors, and inhibits the IL-6-mediated signaling.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Define the therapeutic role and limitations of Opioids in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back:
• Role: Management of severe, acute pain when other analgesics fail.
• Limitation: Lacks anti-inflammatory properties and does not affect the underlying disease process.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 673 (Book Page): [Acetaminophen... lacks anti-inflammatory properties... is inadequate therapy for inflammatory conditions such as RA. Page 676 (Book Page): [Opioids] relieve acute severe pain with remarkable efficacy.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: List the five primary pharmacological classes used in the clinical management of Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA).
back:
- NSAIDs
- Glucocorticoids (Corticosteroids)
- Conventional synthetic DMARDs (csDMARDs)
- Biologic DMARDs (bDMARDs)
- Targeted synthetic DMARDs (tsDMARDs)
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): [These therapies include conventional synthetic (cs) and biologic (b) disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (recently designated csDMARDs and bDMARDs, respectively)... Tofacitinib... is actually a targeted synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD).]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: What is the primary cellular mechanism of Tofacitinib in the treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
- Selectively inhibits the Janus kinase (JAK) family
- Interrupts the JAK-STAT signaling pathway
- Reduces T and B lymphocyte differentiation, proliferation, and inflammatory function
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): [Tofacitinib is a targeted synthetic small molecule (tsDMARD) that selectively inhibits all members of the Janus kinase (JAK... hence interrupting the JAK-STAT signaling pathway... crucial for the differentiation, proliferation, and function of NK cells and T and B lymphocytes.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Contrast the therapeutic goals of NSAIDs versus DMARDs in patients diagnosed with Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back:
- NSAIDs: Rapid relief of acute symptoms (pain/stiffness) and inflammation
- DMARDs: Arrest or slow disease progression and bony damage
- DMARD onset takes 2 weeks to 6 months
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 643 (Book Page): [Reduction of inflammation with NSAIDs often results in relief of pain... The effects of disease-modifying therapies may take 2 weeks to 6 months to become clinically evident.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: A patient fails initial Methotrexate therapy and requires a CD20-targeted biologic. Identify the drug and indication.
back:
- Drug: Rituximab
- Indication: Moderately to severely active RA failing TNF-alpha antagonists
- Mechanism: Depletes CD20 B lymphocytes via cell-mediated and complement-dependent cytotoxicity
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): [Rituximab is a chimeric monoclonal antibody biologic agent that targets CD20 B lymphocytes... indicated for the treatment of moderately to severely active RA in combination with methotrexate in patients with an inadequate response to one or more TNF-α antagonists.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Describe the molecular mechanism of Abatacept in inhibiting the inflammatory cascade of Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back:
- Binds to CD80 and CD86 on antigen-presenting cells
- Prevents binding to CD28 on T cells
- Inhibits T-cell activation (co-stimulation modulation)
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): [Abatacept... binds to CD80 and 86, thereby inhibiting the binding to CD28 and preventing the activation of T cells.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: List the five 'legacy' TNF-alpha blocking biologics currently approved for treating Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back:
- Adalimumab
- Infliximab
- Etanercept
- Golimumab
- Certolizumab
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): [Five “legacy” bDMARDs interfering with TNF-α have been approved for the treatment of RA and other rheumatic diseases]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: What is the biochemical rationale for 'triple therapy' in managing aggressive Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
- Combines Methotrexate, Sulfasalazine, and Hydroxychloroquine
- Provides efficacy comparable to Etanercept/Methotrexate
- Utilizes non-overlapping synthetic DMARD mechanisms to improve clinical outcomes
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 658 (Book Page): [Triple therapy with methotrexate, sulfasalazine, and hydroxychloroquine appears to be as effective as etanercept and methotrexate.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Which biologic agent should be considered for RA patients failing methotrexate by targeting the IL-6 receptor?
back:
- Drug: Tocilizumab
- Mechanism: Binds to soluble and membrane-bound IL-6 receptors
- Blocks T-cell activation and acute-phase protein synthesis
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): [Tocilizumab... binds to soluble and membrane-bound IL-6 receptors, and inhibits the IL-6-mediated signaling via these receptors... involved in... T-cell activation, hepatic acute-phase protein synthesis.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Explain the concept of 'circadian chronotherapy' using low-dose prednisone in RA management.
back:
- Delayed-release prednisone taken at 9-10 PM
- Releases active drug at 2-4 AM
- Targets early morning proinflammatory cytokine surges to reduce morning stiffness
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 658 (Book Page): [A recent approach uses delayed-release prednisone... Taking the drug at 9–10 pm results in a small pulse of prednisone at 2–4 am, decreasing the circadian inflammatory cytokines.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: State the maximum recommended daily dose of prednisone for long-term maintenance in RA.
back:
- Dosage: 7.5 mg daily or less
- Rationale: Minimizes serious toxicities (osteoporosis, Cushingoid effects)
- Goal: Gradual reduction is encouraged once disease is controlled
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 658 (Book Page): [When prednisone is required for long-term therapy, the dosage should not exceed 7.5 mg daily, and gradual reduction of the dose should be encouraged.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Classify the four main categories of DMARDs used in the treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back:
1. Conventional synthetic (csDMARDs)
2. Biologic original (boDMARDs)
3. Biosimilar (bsDMARDs)
4. Targeted synthetic (tsDMARDs)
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): These therapies include conventional synthetic (cs) and biologic (b) disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (recently designated csDMARDs and bDMARDs, respectively). ... bDMARDs are further divided into biological original ... and biosimilar DMARDs. ... Tofacitinib ... is actually a targeted synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD).

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: What is the specific biochemical mechanism of Methotrexate at low doses in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: Inhibition of AICAR transformylase and thymidylate synthetase, leading to extracellular adenosine accumulation which inhibits inflammation.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): Methotrexate’s principal mechanism of action at the low doses used in the rheumatic diseases probably relates to inhibition of amino-imidazolecarboxamide ribonucleotide (AICAR) transformylase and thymidylate synthetase. ... The AMP is released and converted extracellularly to adenosine, which is a potent inhibitor of inflammation.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Contrast the clinical onset of action between NSAIDs and DMARDs in managing RA.
back:
NSAIDs: Prompt relief of symptoms (pain/swelling).
DMARDs: Delayed onset (2 weeks to 6 months) but modify disease progression/bone damage.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): The effects of disease-modifying therapies may take 2 weeks to 6 months to become clinically evident. ... Page 643 (Book Page): Reduction of inflammation with NSAIDs often results in relief of pain for significant periods.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Which class of biologic DMARDs is specifically contraindicated in patients with overt heart failure?
back: TNF-alpha (TNF-α) blocking agents (e.g., Infliximab, Etanercept, Adalimumab).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): In patients with borderline or overt heart failure (HF), TNF-α–blocking agents can exacerbate HF.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Identify the primary molecular target inhibited by the targeted synthetic DMARD Tofacitinib.
back: Janus kinase (JAK) family, specifically JAK3 and JAK1, interrupting the JAK-STAT signaling pathway.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): Tofacitinib is a targeted synthetic small molecule (tsDMARD) that selectively inhibits all members of the Janus kinase (JAK; see Chapter 2) family to varying degrees. At therapeutic doses, tofacitinib exerts its effect mainly by inhibiting JAK3, and to a lesser extent JAK1.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: List the five "legacy" TNF-alpha blocking agents approved for Rheumatoid Arthritis therapy.
back:
1. Adalimumab
2. Infliximab
3. Etanercept
4. Certolizumab
5. Golimumab
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): Five “legacy” bDMARDs interfering with TNF-α have been approved for the treatment of RA and other rheumatic diseases (Figure 36–4). ... Adalimumab, Certolizumab, Etanercept, Golimumab, Infliximab.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Why are low-dose corticosteroids utilized as "bridge therapy" in early RA management?
back: They provide prompt, dramatic anti-inflammatory effects and slow bone erosions while waiting for slower-acting DMARDs to take effect.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 658 (Book Page): Corticosteroids ... effects are prompt and dramatic, and they are capable of slowing the appearance of new bone erosions. ... [Used] during periods of exacerbation.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: A patient on Leflunomide becomes pregnant. What drug is used to rapidly clear the active metabolite?
back: Cholestyramine (enhances biliary excretion and total clearance).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): Cholestyramine can enhance leflunomide excretion and increases total clearance by approximately 50%. ... This drug is contraindicated in pregnancy.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: What is the mechanism of action for the biologic agent Tocilizumab in RA treatment?
back: Binds to both soluble and membrane-bound Interleukin-6 (IL-6) receptors, inhibiting IL-6-mediated proinflammatory signaling.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): Tocilizumab, a newer biologic humanized antibody, binds to soluble and membrane-bound IL-6 receptors, and inhibits the IL-6-mediated signaling via these receptors.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Which conventional synthetic DMARD is the recognized first-line therapy for Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: Methotrexate.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): Methotrexate, a synthetic nonbiologic antimetabolite, is the first-line csDMARD for treating RA and is used in 50–70% of patients.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Classify the five main functional categories of drugs used in Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) management.
back:
1. NSAIDs
2. Corticosteroids
3. Conventional synthetic DMARDs (csDMARDs)
4. Biologic DMARDs (bDMARDs)
5. Targeted synthetic DMARDs (tsDMARDs)
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): [Source 36] These therapies include conventional synthetic (cs) and biologic (b) disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (recently designated csDMARDs and bDMARDs, respectively). Tofacitinib, though marketed as a biologic, is actually a targeted synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD).

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: List four common conventional synthetic DMARDs (csDMARDs) utilized as first-line therapy for RA.
back:
1. Methotrexate (Gold standard)
2. Sulfasalazine
3. Hydroxychloroquine
4. Leflunomide
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): [Source 36] The conventional synthetic agents include small molecule drugs such as methotrexate, azathioprine, chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine, cyclophosphamide, cyclosporine, leflunomide, mycophenolate mofetil, and sulfasalazine.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Name the five 'legacy' TNF-α blocking biologic DMARDs approved for treating RA.
back:
1. Adalimumab
2. Infliximab
3. Etanercept
4. Golimumab
5. Certolizumab
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): [Source 36] Five “legacy” bDMARDs interfering with TNF-α have been approved for the treatment of RA and other rheumatic diseases.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Which drug represents the Targeted Synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD) class, and what is its specific molecular target?
back: Drug: Tofacitinib. Target: Janus kinase (JAK) family (primarily JAK3 and JAK1).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): [Source 36] Tofacitinib is a targeted synthetic small molecule (tsDMARD) that selectively inhibits all members of the Janus kinase (JAK) family... mainly by inhibiting JAK3, and to a lesser extent JAK1.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Contrast the biological targets of Abatacept and Rituximab in the treatment of RA.
back:
1. Abatacept: T-cell costimulation modulator (binds CD80/86).
2. Rituximab: B-cell cytotoxic agent (targets CD20 B lymphocytes).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): [Source 36] The bDMARDs approved for RA include a T-cell–modulating biologic (abatacept), a B-cell cytotoxic agent (rituximab).

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: What is the primary limitation of NSAIDs as a monotherapy in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: NSAIDs provide analgesic and anti-inflammatory relief but do not alter the disease course or prevent bony damage/destruction.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 644 (Book Page): [Source 36] Although these drugs effectively inhibit inflammation, there is no evidence that... they alter the course of any arthritic disorder.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Identify the components of the high-yield 'Triple Therapy' regimen used in conventional RA treatment.
back:
1. Methotrexate
2. Sulfasalazine
3. Hydroxychloroquine
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 658 (Book Page): [Source 36] Triple therapy with methotrexate, sulfasalazine, and hydroxychloroquine appears to be as effective as etanercept and methotrexate.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: What unique therapeutic benefit do corticosteroids provide when starting DMARD therapy in early RA?
back: They act as 'bridge therapy' providing rapid anti-inflammatory effects and slowing bone erosions while waiting for DMARDs to take effect.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 643 (Book Page): [Source 36] Although there are data indicating that low-dose corticosteroids have disease-modifying properties, particularly in the early phase of RA, their toxicity makes them less favored than other medications.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: List the three Interleukin-1 (IL-1) inhibitors approved for RA or autoinflammatory syndromes.
back:
1. Anakinra
2. Canakinumab
3. Rilonacept
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): [Source 36] IL-1 inhibitors: Anakinra... Canakinumab... Rilonacept.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: When is the use of nonopioid analgesics like Acetaminophen preferred over NSAIDs in RA patients?
back: When an anti-inflammatory effect is not necessary, or in patients with aspirin allergy, peptic ulcers, or bronchospasm history.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 659 (Book Page): [Source 36] Acetaminophen is the preferred drug in patients allergic to aspirin, when salicylates are poorly tolerated... history of peptic ulcer, and in those in whom bronchospasm is precipitated by aspirin.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Classify the four major categories of drugs used to treat Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA).
back:
* NSAIDs (symptom relief)
* Glucocorticoids (bridge therapy)
* DMARDs (conventional synthetic and biologic)
* Targeted Synthetic DMARDs (JAK inhibitors).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): The treatment of patients with inflammation involves two primary goals: first, the relief of symptoms... and second, the slowing or arrest of the tissue-damaging process... NSAIDs... glucocorticoids... DMARDs.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: What is the primary mechanism of action for Methotrexate at low doses used in RA?
back:
* Inhibits AICAR transformylase
* Increases extracellular adenosine concentration
* Adenosine acts as a potent anti-inflammatory mediator.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): Methotrexate’s principal mechanism of action... relates to inhibition of amino-imidazolecarboxamide ribonucleotide (AICAR) transformylase... leads to an accumulation of AMP... converted extracellularly to adenosine.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Distinguish between conventional synthetic DMARDs (csDMARDs) and biologic DMARDs (bDMARDs).
back:
* csDMARDs: Small molecule drugs (e.g., Methotrexate, Sulfasalazine)
* bDMARDs: Large-molecule proteins/monoclonal antibodies targeting specific cytokines or cells (e.g., TNF-α inhibitors).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): These therapies include conventional synthetic (cs) and biologic (b) disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs... csDMARDs include small molecule drugs... Biologics are large-molecule therapeutic agents, usually proteins.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: What mandatory screening must be performed before starting a patient on Infliximab or other bDMARDs?
back:
* Latent Tuberculosis (Mantoux/IGRA)
* Viral Hepatitis (HBV/HCV)
* Reason: High risk of reactivating dormant macrophage-dependent infections.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): all patients should be screened for latent or active tuberculosis before starting TNF-α–blocking agents... also associated with increased risk of HBV reactivation.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Describe the active metabolite and enzymatic target of the csDMARD Leflunomide.
back:
* Active Metabolite: A77-1726
* Enzyme Target: Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase
* Result: Arrests T-cell proliferation by decreasing ribonucleotide synthesis.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): Leflunomide... conversion... to its active metabolite, A77-1726. This metabolite inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, leading to a decrease in ribonucleotide synthesis.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: What specific toxicity requires annual monitoring in patients taking Hydroxychloroquine for RA?
back:
* Retinal toxicity (maculopathy)
* Monitoring: Annual ophthalmologic examination to check for tissue binding in melanin-containing structures.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 650 (Book Page): ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months is advised [for hydroxychloroquine]... very extensively tissue-bound, particularly in melanin-containing tissues such as the eyes.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Why are glucocorticoids clinically used as 'bridge therapy' in newly diagnosed RA patients?
back:
* DMARDs take 2 weeks to 6 months to work
* Glucocorticoids provide prompt anti-inflammatory relief and slow bone erosion until DMARDs reach therapeutic levels.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): The effects of disease-modifying therapies may take 2 weeks to 6 months to become clinically evident... [Page 658 (Book Page)] Corticosteroids... effects are prompt and dramatic, and they are capable of slowing the appearance of new bone erosions.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Classify Tofacitinib and specify its intracellular signaling target.
back:
* Classification: Targeted Synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD)
* Target: Janus Kinase (JAK) family (primarily JAK3 and JAK1)
* Action: Interrupts the JAK-STAT signaling pathway.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): Tofacitinib... is actually a targeted synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD)... selectively inhibits all members of the Janus kinase (JAK) family... mainly by inhibiting JAK3.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: How is Sulfasalazine metabolized to its active moiety for RA treatment?
back:
* Reduced by intestinal bacteria into Sulfapyridine and 5-aminosalicylic acid
* Sulfapyridine is the active component for RA.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): Sulfasalazine... metabolized to sulfapyridine and 5-aminosalicylic acid. The sulfapyridine is probably the active moiety when treating RA.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Which specific T-cell co-stimulation interaction is blocked by Abatacept?
back:
* Blocks CD28 (on T-cells) from binding to CD80/86 (on APCs)
* Result: Prevents T-cell activation in the RA inflammatory cascade.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): Abatacept (which contains the endogenous ligand CTLA-4) binds to CD80 and 86, thereby inhibiting the binding to CD28 and preventing the activation of T cells.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Classify the four main pharmacological categories used in the management of Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA).
back:
1. NSAIDs (symptomatic relief)
2. Glucocorticoids (anti-inflammatory/bridge therapy)
3. DMARDs (conventional synthetic and biological)
4. Targeted synthetic DMARDs (JAK inhibitors)
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): [The treatment of patients with inflammation involves two primary goals: first, the relief of symptoms... and second, the slowing or arrest of the tissue-damaging process.] Page 663 (Book Page): [These therapies include conventional synthetic (cs) and biologic (b) disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs... Tofacitinib... is actually a targeted synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD).]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: What is the primary mechanism and clinical limitation of NSAIDs in RA therapy?
back:
Mechanism: Inhibition of prostaglandin biosynthesis.
Limitation: They relieve pain and inflammation but do not alter the course of the disease or prevent bone damage.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 658 (Book Page): [NSAID anti-inflammatory activity is mediated chiefly through inhibition of prostaglandin biosynthesis... there is no evidence that... they alter the course of any arthritic disorder.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Distinguish between csDMARDs and bDMARDs based on their chemical nature and production.
back:
csDMARDs: Small molecule synthetic drugs (e.g., Methotrexate).
bDMARDs: Large-molecule proteins/monoclonal antibodies produced via recombinant DNA technology (e.g., TNF-α blockers).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 663 (Book Page): [These therapies include conventional synthetic (cs) and biologic (b) disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs... Biologics are large-molecule therapeutic agents, usually proteins, which are often produced by recombinant DNA technology.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Which drug transition is indicated for an RA patient with high GI bleeding risk on nonselective NSAIDs?
back: Switch to Celecoxib (selective COX-2 inhibitor) or use a nonselective NSAID combined with a proton pump inhibitor (e.g., Omeprazole) or Misoprostol.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 663 (Book Page): [Celecoxib or a nonselective NSAID plus omeprazole or misoprostol may be appropriate in patients at highest risk for GI bleeding; in this subpopulation of patients, they are cost-effective.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Describe the mechanism of action of Leflunomide in arresting the immune response in RA.
back: Inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH), decreasing ribonucleotide synthesis. This leads to T-cell proliferation arrest in the G1 phase and reduced B-cell autoantibody production.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 665 (Book Page): [This metabolite inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, leading to a decrease in ribonucleotide synthesis and the arrest of stimulated cells in the G1 phase of cell growth. Consequently, leflunomide inhibits T-cell proliferation.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: List three distinct 'legacy' biologic DMARDs that target Tumor Necrosis Factor-alpha (TNF-α).
back:
1. Adalimumab
2. Infliximab
3. Etanercept
(Others include Certolizumab and Golimumab).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 667 (Book Page): [Five “legacy” bDMARDs interfering with TNF-α have been approved for the treatment of RA... Adalimumab, Certolizumab, Etanercept, Golimumab, and Infliximab.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: How does low-dose Methotrexate suppress inflammation in rheumatoid synovitis?
back: Inhibits AICAR transformylase, causing intracellular AICAR accumulation. This leads to increased extracellular Adenosine, which acts as a potent inhibitor of neutrophil and macrophage function.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 665 (Book Page): [Methotrexate’s principal mechanism... relates to inhibition of amino-imidazolecarboxamide ribonucleotide (AICAR) transformylase... AICAR... inhibits AMP deaminase, leading to an accumulation of AMP... converted extracellularly to adenosine, which is a potent inhibitor of inflammation.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Why is Leflunomide avoided in pregnancy, and how is it cleared in emergencies?
back: It is highly teratogenic. Due to its long half-life (19 days), Cholestyramine is administered to enhance excretion and increase total clearance by 50%.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 665 (Book Page): [Leflunomide... has a mean plasma half-life of 19 days... Cholestyramine can enhance leflunomide excretion and increases total clearance by approximately 50%... This drug is contraindicated in pregnancy.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Explain the 'bridge therapy' role of low-dose corticosteroids in early RA management.
back: Corticosteroids provide prompt symptomatic relief and slow bone erosion during the 2-week to 6-month delay required for DMARDs to become clinically effective.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): [low-dose corticosteroids have disease-modifying properties, particularly in the early phase of RA...] Page 663 (Book Page): [The effects of disease-modifying therapies may take 2 weeks to 6 months to become clinically evident.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Define the classification and molecular target of Tofacitinib.
back:
Classification: Targeted synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD).
Target: Inhibits the Janus kinase (JAK) family, interrupting the JAK-STAT signaling pathway crucial for lymphocyte function.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 663 (Book Page): [Tofacitinib, though marketed as a biologic, is actually a targeted synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD).] Page 670 (Book Page): [selectively inhibits all members of the Janus kinase (JAK) family... interrupting the JAK-STAT signaling pathway.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Classify the four primary drug categories used to treat Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA).
back:
1. NSAIDs (Symptomatic relief)
2. Corticosteroids (Bridge therapy)
3. DMARDs (Conventional synthetic, biologic, and targeted synthetic)
4. Adjunctive agents (e.g., Opioids for refractory pain)
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): [The treatment of patients with inflammation involves two primary goals: first, the relief of symptoms... and second, the slowing or arrest of the tissue-damaging process... these include NSAIDs, glucocorticoids, and DMARDs.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Contrast the clinical utility of NSAIDs versus DMARDs in RA management.
back:
• NSAIDs: Provide rapid analgesia and anti-inflammatory relief but do not alter disease course.
• DMARDs: Slow or arrest tissue damage and bony erosions; effects take 2 weeks to 6 months to manifest.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 658 (Book Page): [All newer NSAIDs are analgesic, anti-inflammatory... there is no evidence that... they alter the course of any arthritic disorder... DMARDs might arrest—or at least slow—this progression.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: List the four most common Conventional Synthetic DMARDs (csDMARDs).
back:
1. Methotrexate (First-line/Gold standard)
2. Sulfasalazine
3. Hydroxychloroquine
4. Leflunomide
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 663 (Book Page): [The conventional synthetic agents include small molecule drugs such as methotrexate, azathioprine, chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine, cyclophosphamide, cyclosporine, leflunomide... and sulfasalazine.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Classify Biologic DMARDs (bDMARDs) by their molecular targets in RA.
back:
• TNF-α Inhibitors (e.g., Adalimumab)
• T-cell Modulators (Abatacept)
• B-cell Cytotoxics (Rituximab)
• IL-6 Inhibitors (Tocilizumab)
• IL-1 Inhibitors (Anakinra)
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 663 (Book Page): [The bDMARDs approved for RA include a T-cell–modulating biologic (abatacept), a B-cell cytotoxic agent (rituximab), an anti–IL-6 receptor antibody (tocilizumab), IL-1–inhibiting agents (anakinra), and the TNF-α–blocking agents.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: What drug serves as a 'Targeted Synthetic' DMARD (tsDMARD) by inhibiting Janus Kinase (JAK)?
back: Tofacitinib. It interrupts the JAK-STAT signaling pathway crucial for lymphocyte proliferation and function.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 670 (Book Page): [Tofacitinib is a targeted synthetic small molecule (tsDMARD) that selectively inhibits all members of the Janus kinase (JAK) family... interrupting the JAK-STAT signaling pathway.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Define 'Bridge Therapy' involving corticosteroids in early Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back: The use of low-dose glucocorticoids to provide immediate anti-inflammatory effects while waiting for slow-acting DMARDs (like Methotrexate) to achieve clinical efficacy.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): [Although there are data indicating that low-dose corticosteroids have disease-modifying properties, particularly in the early phase of RA... they continue to have a significant role.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Name the five 'legacy' TNF-α blocking agents used in Pakistani clinical practice.
back:
1. Adalimumab
2. Infliximab
3. Etanercept
4. Golimumab
5. Certolizumab
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 667 (Book Page): [Five “legacy” bDMARDs interfering with TNF-α have been approved for the treatment of RA... Adalimumab, Infliximab, Etanercept, Golimumab, Certolizumab.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Which RA medication should be prioritized for a patient with high disease activity failing Methotrexate?
back: TNF-α inhibitors (often used in combination with Methotrexate) or another biologic like Abatacept or Rituximab.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 666 (Book Page): [Rituximab is indicated for the treatment of moderately to severely active RA in combination with methotrexate in patients with an inadequate response to one or more TNF-α antagonists.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: How does the mechanism of Abatacept differ from Rituximab in RA?
back:
• Abatacept: Inhibits T-cell activation by binding CD80/86 on antigen-presenting cells.
• Rituximab: Targets CD20 on B-lymphocytes to cause cell depletion via cytotoxicity.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 663 (Book Page)/666: [Abatacept... inhibits the activation of T cells... Rituximab is a chimeric monoclonal antibody biologic agent that targets CD20 B lymphocytes.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: What is the specific clinical role of Opioids in Rheumatoid Arthritis management?
back: Limited to short-term or adjunctive use for severe, refractory pain that is not controlled by anti-inflammatory or disease-modifying agents.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 553 (Book Page)/657: [The nonopioid analgesics... are appropriate for both acute and chronic inflammatory conditions. Opioids (e.g. Morphine) relieve acute severe pain with remarkable efficacy.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Classify the four primary groups of drugs used in the pharmacological management of Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA).
back:
- NSAIDs (symptomatic relief)
- Corticosteroids (anti-inflammatory/bridge)
- DMARDs (Disease-Modifying Antirheumatic Drugs)
- Adjunctive analgesics (e.g., Opioids)
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): [The treatment of patients with inflammation involves two primary goals: first, the relief of symptoms... and second, the slowing or arrest of the tissue-damaging process. Reduction of inflammation with NSAIDs... The glucocorticoids also have powerful anti-inflammatory effects... Another important group of agents are characterized as disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs)]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: What is the primary mechanism of action for Methotrexate at the low doses typically used for RA?
back:
- Inhibits AICAR transformylase and thymidylate synthetase
- Leads to intracellular accumulation of AICAR
- Results in extracellular adenosine release, which potently inhibits inflammation
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 665 (Book Page): [Methotrexate’s principal mechanism of action at the low doses used in the rheumatic diseases probably relates to inhibition of amino-imidazolecarboxamide ribonucleotide (AICAR) transformylase and thymidylate synthetase... AICAR... inhibits AMP deaminase, leading to an accumulation of AMP. The AMP is released and converted extracellularly to adenosine, which is a potent inhibitor of inflammation.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Contrast NSAIDs and DMARDs regarding their ability to modify the clinical course of Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back:
- NSAIDs: Provide symptomatic relief (pain/inflammation) only; do NOT alter disease course.
- DMARDs: Interfere with basic inflammatory mechanisms to slow or arrest bone damage and disease progression.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 658 (Book Page): [Although these drugs effectively inhibit inflammation, there is no evidence that—in contrast to drugs such as methotrexate, biologics, and other DMARDs—they [NSAIDs] alter the course of any arthritic disorder.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: What mandatory screening must be performed before initiating a TNF-α blocking agent like Infliximab?
back:
- Screening for latent Tuberculosis (TBT/PPD)
- Screening for Viral Hepatitis (HBV)
- Rationale: High risk of reactivation for these infections.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 670 (Book Page): [The risk of bacterial infections and macrophage-dependent infection (including tuberculosis, fungal, and other opportunistic infections) is increased... all patients should be screened for latent or active tuberculosis before starting TNF-α–blocking agents... associated with increased risk of HBV reactivation; screening for HBV is important.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: State the metabolic bioactivation and specific enzyme target of the DMARD Leflunomide.
back:
- Bioactivation: Converted to active metabolite A77-1726
- Target: Inhibits Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase
- Result: Arrests T-cell proliferation by decreasing ribonucleotide synthesis.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 665 (Book Page): [Leflunomide... undergoes rapid conversion... to its active metabolite, A77-1726. This metabolite inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, leading to a decrease in ribonucleotide synthesis and the arrest of stimulated cells in the G1 phase... inhibits T-cell proliferation.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Identify three legacy TNF-α blocking biologics approved for Rheumatoid Arthritis management.
back:
- Adalimumab
- Etanercept
- Infliximab
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 667 (Book Page): [Five “legacy” bDMARDs interfering with TNF-α have been approved... [Figure 36-4 includes Adalimumab, Infliximab, Etanercept, Golimumab, Certolizumab]]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Explain the "bridge therapy" concept of using corticosteroids with DMARDs in early RA.
back:
- Corticosteroids provide prompt symptomatic relief
- DMARDs take 2 weeks to 6 months for clinical evidence of effect
- Steroids are used until DMARDs reach therapeutic efficacy.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 663 (Book Page): [The effects of disease-modifying therapies may take 2 weeks to 6 months to become clinically evident... [Page 672 (Book Page)] Corticosteroids... effects are prompt and dramatic... may be administered... during periods of exacerbation.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Classify Tofacitinib and describe its unique intracellular signaling target in RA.
back:
- Class: Targeted synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD)
- Target: Janus kinase (JAK) family (primarily JAK3 and JAK1)
- Effect: Interrupts the JAK-STAT signaling pathway for cytokine transcription.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 670 (Book Page): [Tofacitinib, though marketed as a biologic, is actually a targeted synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD)... selectively inhibits all members of the Janus kinase (JAK) family... mainly by inhibiting JAK3, and to a lesser extent JAK1, hence interrupting the JAK-STAT signaling pathway.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Describe the mechanism by which Abatacept inhibits T-cell activation in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back:
- Contains CTLA-4 domain
- Binds to CD80 and CD86 on Antigen Presenting Cells (APCs)
- Prevents binding to T-cell CD28, blocking the co-stimulation signal.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 663 (Book Page): [Abatacept (which contains the endogenous ligand CTLA-4) binds to CD80 and 86, thereby inhibiting the binding to CD28 and preventing the activation of T cells.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Which biologic agent used in RA therapy specifically targets CD20 on B-lymphocytes?
back:
- Rituximab
- Action: Chimeric monoclonal antibody that depletes B cells via cytotoxicity and apoptosis.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 666 (Book Page): [Rituximab is a chimeric monoclonal antibody biologic agent that targets CD20 B lymphocytes... Depletion of these cells takes place through cell-mediated and complement-dependent cytotoxicity and stimulation of cell apoptosis.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: How are DMARDs categorized in the pharmacological management of Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA)?
back:
1. Conventional synthetic (csDMARDs): e.g., Methotrexate.
2. Biologic (bDMARDs): e.g., Infliximab (TNF blockers).
3. Targeted synthetic (tsDMARDs): e.g., Tofacitinib (JAK inhibitors).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): [These therapies include conventional synthetic (cs) and biologic (b) disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs... Tofacitinib, though marketed as a biologic, is actually a targeted synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD).]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: What is the specific molecular mechanism of the tsDMARD Tofacitinib in treating RA?
back: It selectively inhibits the Janus kinase (JAK) family, primarily JAK3 and JAK1. This interrupts the JAK-STAT signaling pathway, blocking cytokine-driven T and B lymphocyte proliferation.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): [Tofacitinib is a targeted synthetic small molecule (tsDMARD) that selectively inhibits all members of the Janus kinase (JAK) family... hence interrupting the JAK-STAT signaling pathway.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Contrast the therapeutic goals of NSAIDs versus DMARDs in Rheumatoid Arthritis management.
back: NSAIDs provide rapid symptomatic relief of pain and inflammation but do not stop joint destruction. DMARDs slow or arrest the progression of bone damage and joint deformity.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 643 (Book Page): [Reduction of inflammation with NSAIDs often results in relief of pain... DMARDs... decrease inflammation, improve symptoms, and slow the bone damage associated with RA.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Which drug regimen is recommended for an RA patient at high risk for GI bleeding?
back: Celecoxib (selective COX-2 inhibitor) or a nonselective NSAID combined with a proton pump inhibitor (e.g., Omeprazole) or Misoprostol.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): [Celecoxib is probably safest for patients at high risk for GI bleeding... Celecoxib or a nonselective NSAID plus omeprazole or misoprostol may be appropriate in patients at highest risk for GI bleeding.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: What is the high-yield mechanism of low-dose Methotrexate as an anti-inflammatory in RA?
back: Inhibition of AICAR transformylase leads to extracellular accumulation of Adenosine. Adenosine acts as a potent inhibitor of neutrophil, macrophage, and lymphocyte inflammatory functions.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): [Methotrexate’s principal mechanism... relates to inhibition of amino-imidazolecarboxamide ribonucleotide (AICAR) transformylase... converted extracellularly to adenosine, which is a potent inhibitor of inflammation.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: List the five 'legacy' TNF-alpha blocking bDMARDs used for RA.
back:
1. Adalimumab.
2. Infliximab.
3. Etanercept.
4. Certolizumab.
5. Golimumab.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): [Five 'legacy' bDMARDs interfering with TNF-α have been approved... [Figure 36-4 lists Adalimumab, Infliximab, Etanercept, Golimumab, and Certolizumab]]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: How does the csDMARD Leflunomide arrest stimulated T-cell proliferation?
back: Its active metabolite (A77-1726) inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase. This depletes ribonucleotide synthesis, arresting cells in the G1 phase of the growth cycle.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): [This metabolite inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, leading to a decrease in ribonucleotide synthesis and the arrest of stimulated cells in the G1 phase of cell growth.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: What is the specific clinical indication for the B-cell cytotoxic biologic Rituximab in RA?
back: Moderately to severely active RA, in combination with Methotrexate, specifically for patients who have failed one or more TNF-alpha antagonists.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): [Rituximab is indicated for the treatment of moderately to severely active RA in combination with methotrexate in patients with an inadequate response to one or more TNF-α antagonists.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Explain the benefit of 'chronotherapy' with delayed-release Prednisone in RA patients.
back: Dosing at 9–10 PM releases drug at 2–4 AM. This prevents the early morning spike of proinflammatory cytokines, effectively reducing morning stiffness and joint pain.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 658 (Book Page): [Taking the drug at 9–10 pm results in a small pulse of prednisone at 2–4 am, decreasing the circadian inflammatory cytokines.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Why are nonacetylated salicylates preferred over Aspirin in patients with asthma or bleeding risks?
back: Unlike Aspirin, drugs like Sodium Salicylate or Salicyl Salicylate do not inhibit platelet aggregation and are less likely to trigger bronchospasm in aspirin-sensitive patients.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 645 (Book Page): [All nonacetylated salicylates... do not inhibit platelet aggregation. They may be preferable... in patients with asthma, those with bleeding tendencies.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: What are the primary drug classes used in the management of Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
- NSAIDs
- Corticosteroids
- csDMARDs
- bDMARDs/tsDMARDs
- Opioids
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): [The treatment of patients with inflammation involves two primary goals... relief of symptoms with NSAIDs... glucocorticoids... disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs) including biologics.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: By what mechanism do NSAIDs provide symptomatic relief in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
- Inhibition of prostaglandin biosynthesis via COX enzymes
- Reduces inflammation and pain
- Does not alter disease course
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 658 (Book Page): [NSAID anti-inflammatory activity is mediated chiefly through inhibition of prostaglandin biosynthesis (Figure 36–2).]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: How do DMARDs differ functionally from NSAIDs in RA therapy?
back:
- NSAIDs: Relieve symptoms/pain only
- DMARDs: Slow or arrest tissue-damaging processes and bone damage
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): [They (DMARDs) decrease inflammation, improve symptoms, and slow the bone damage associated with RA. They affect more basic inflammatory mechanisms than do glucocorticoids or the NSAIDs.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: A patient fails initial NSAID therapy for RA; which drug is the first-line csDMARD?
back:
- Methotrexate (MTX)
- Used in 50–70% of patients
- Potent synthetic nonbiologic antimetabolite
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 665 (Book Page): [Methotrexate, a synthetic nonbiologic antimetabolite, is the first-line csDMARD for treating RA and is used in 50–70% of patients.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Classify the five 'legacy' biologic DMARDs (bDMARDs) that interfere with TNF-α.
back:
- Adalimumab
- Infliximab
- Etanercept
- Golimumab
- Certolizumab
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 667 (Book Page): [Five “legacy” bDMARDs interfering with TNF-α have been approved for the treatment of RA... (Adalimumab, Infliximab, Etanercept, Golimumab, Certolizumab).]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: List the four common conventional synthetic DMARDs (csDMARDs) used in RA.
back:
- Methotrexate
- Sulfasalazine
- Hydroxychloroquine
- Leflunomide
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 664 (Book Page): [The conventional synthetic agents include small molecule drugs such as methotrexate, azathioprine, chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine... leflunomide... and sulfasalazine.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: What unique therapeutic benefit do low-dose corticosteroids offer in early RA?
back:
- Possess disease-modifying properties
- Arrest progression in early phases
- Potent anti-inflammatory action
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): [low-dose corticosteroids have disease-modifying properties, particularly in the early phase of RA... they continue to have a significant role.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: A patient requires 'targeted synthetic' therapy for RA; which drug fits this classification?
back:
- Tofacitinib
- Mechanism: Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor
- Category: tsDMARD
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 664 (Book Page): [Tofacitinib, though marketed as a biologic, is actually a targeted synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD).]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: What is the mechanism of action for the biologic agent Abatacept?
back:
- T-cell co-stimulation modulator
- Binds to CD80/86 on APCs
- Inhibits binding to CD28, preventing T-cell activation
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 664 (Book Page): [Abatacept is a co-stimulation modulator biologic that inhibits the activation of T cells... binds to CD80 and 86, thereby inhibiting the binding to CD28.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: In which scenario is the use of Opioid Agonists indicated in RA?
back:
- Relief of acute severe pain
- Used when other analgesics fail
- Does not treat underlying inflammation
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 567 (Book Page): [Morphine, the prototypic opioid agonist, has long been known to relieve acute severe pain with remarkable efficacy.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Name the four primary conventional synthetic DMARDs (csDMARDs) used in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back:
1. Methotrexate (First-line drug)
2. Sulfasalazine
3. Hydroxychloroquine
4. Leflunomide
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): The conventional synthetic agents include small molecule drugs such as methotrexate, azathioprine, chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine, cyclophosphamide, cyclosporine, leflunomide, mycophenolate mofetil, and sulfasalazine.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: What is the primary mechanism of action for the csDMARD Leflunomide?
back: Leflunomide's active metabolite (A77-1726) inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH). This decreases ribonucleotide synthesis and arrests T-cell proliferation in the G1 phase.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): This metabolite inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, leading to a decrease in ribonucleotide synthesis and the arrest of stimulated cells in the G1 phase of cell growth.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Classify the biologics (bDMARDs) used in RA based on targets other than TNF-α.
back:
1. T-cell modulator: Abatacept
2. B-cell cytotoxic: Rituximab
3. IL-6 inhibitor: Tocilizumab
4. IL-1 inhibitor: Anakinra
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): The bDMARDs approved for RA include a T-cell–modulating biologic (abatacept), a B-cell cytotoxic agent (rituximab), an anti–IL-6 receptor antibody (tocilizumab), IL-1–inhibiting agents (anakinra, rilonacept, canakinumab).

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
coreConcept: NSAID Management in High-Risk RA Patients
front: Q: Which NSAID strategy is preferred for an RA patient with a history of GI bleeding?
back: Celecoxib (selective COX-2 inhibitor) is preferred. It should be combined with a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) like Omeprazole or Misoprostol for maximum GI protection.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 659 (Book Page): The relatively expensive, selective COX-2 inhibitor celecoxib is probably safest for patients at high risk for GI bleeding... Celecoxib or a nonselective NSAID plus omeprazole or misoprostol may be appropriate.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Explain the anti-inflammatory mechanism of low-dose Methotrexate in RA treatment.
back: Inhibits AICAR transformylase, causing intracellular AICAR accumulation. This leads to increased extracellular release of adenosine, which acts as a potent anti-inflammatory mediator.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): inhibition of amino-imidazolecarboxamide ribonucleotide (AICAR) transformylase... AICAR... inhibits AMP deaminase, leading to an accumulation of AMP. The AMP is released and converted extracellularly to adenosine, which is a potent inhibitor of inflammation.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: List the five "legacy" TNF-α blocking agents approved for Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back:
1. Adalimumab
2. Infliximab
3. Etanercept
4. Certolizumab
5. Golimumab
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): Five “legacy” bDMARDs interfering with TNF-α have been approved for the treatment of RA and other rheumatic diseases.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Describe the mechanism of action for Abatacept in RA therapy.
back: A costimulation modulator that binds to CD80/CD86 on antigen-presenting cells. This blocks binding to CD28 on T cells, preventing T-cell activation.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): Abatacept... binds to CD80 and 86, thereby inhibiting the binding to CD28 and preventing the activation of T cells.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: How is Rituximab used in RA management, including required pretreatment?
back: Used for RA refractory to TNF-antagonists. Pretreatment with IV Methylprednisolone, Acetaminophen, and Antihistamines is mandatory to reduce infusion reactions.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): Rituximab is indicated... in patients with an inadequate response to one or more TNF-α antagonists... Pretreatment with acetaminophen, an antihistamine, and intravenous glucocorticoids... decreases the incidence and severity of infusion reactions.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Classify Tofacitinib and state its primary molecular mechanism.
back: Targeted Synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD). It is a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor that interrupts the JAK-STAT signaling pathway (primarily JAK3 and JAK1).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): Tofacitinib is a targeted synthetic small molecule (tsDMARD) that selectively inhibits all members of the Janus kinase (JAK) family... mainly by inhibiting JAK3, and to a lesser extent JAK1.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Classify the analgesics and opioids used for symptomatic relief in RA.
back:
1. Mild/Moderate pain: Acetaminophen
2. Severe/Refractory pain: Opioids (Morphine, Codeine)
3. Centrally acting: Tramadol
Note: These provide analgesia but lack anti-inflammatory or disease-modifying effects.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 659 (Book Page): Acetaminophen is one of the most important drugs... for mild to moderate pain when an anti-inflammatory effect is not necessary... Tramadol is a centrally acting synthetic analgesic, structurally related to opioids.

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Classify the Conventional Synthetic DMARDs (csDMARDs) commonly used in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back:
• Methotrexate (First-line agent)
• Sulfasalazine
• Hydroxychloroquine
• Leflunomide
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): [The conventional synthetic agents include small molecule drugs such as methotrexate, azathioprine, chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine, cyclophosphamide, cyclosporine, leflunomide, mycophenolate mofetil, and sulfasalazine.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: What is the primary mechanism of action for Methotrexate in treating Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
• Inhibits AICAR transformylase
• Leads to extracellular Adenosine accumulation
• Adenosine acts as a potent inhibitor of inflammation
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): [Methotrexate’s principal mechanism of action at the low doses used in the rheumatic diseases probably relates to inhibition of amino-imidazolecarboxamide ribonucleotide (AICAR) transformylase... The AMP is released and converted extracellularly to adenosine, which is a potent inhibitor of inflammation.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Contrast the clinical utility of NSAIDs versus DMARDs in RA management.
back:
• NSAIDs: Provide immediate symptomatic relief (pain/stiffness) but do not arrest disease.
• DMARDs: Slow or arrest tissue-damaging processes and bone erosion.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 658 (Book Page): [there is no evidence that... they [NSAIDs] alter the course of any arthritic disorder. ...biologics (a subset of the DMARDs). They decrease inflammation, improve symptoms, and slow the bone damage associated with RA.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Which B-cell cytotoxic biologic is indicated for RA patients failing TNF-α antagonist therapy?
back:
• Rituximab
• Usually administered as two intravenous infusions separated by 2 weeks
• Given in combination with Methotrexate
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): [Rituximab is indicated for the treatment of moderately to severely active RA in combination with methotrexate in patients with an inadequate response to one or more TNF-α antagonists.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: How does the active metabolite of Leflunomide (A77-1726) inhibit T-cell proliferation?
back:
• Inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase
• Decreases ribonucleotide synthesis
• Arrests stimulated cells in the G1 phase of the cell cycle
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): [This metabolite inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, leading to a decrease in ribonucleotide synthesis and the arrest of stimulated cells in the G1 phase of cell growth. Consequently, leflunomide inhibits T-cell proliferation.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: What is the mandatory screening requirement before starting RA patients on TNF-α blocking agents?
back:
• Screening for latent tuberculosis (TB)
• Screening for viral hepatitis
• Reasoning: TNF is critical for macrophage-dependent infection control.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 669 (Book Page): [The risk of bacterial infections and macrophage-dependent infection (including tuberculosis, fungal, and other opportunistic infections) is increased... all patients should be screened for latent or active tuberculosis before starting TNF-α–blocking agents.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Why is Celecoxib preferred over Naproxen for RA patients with a history of GI ulcers?
back:
• Selective COX-2 inhibition spares gastric COX-1
• Reduced incidence of endoscopic ulcers
• Does not affect platelet aggregation
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 658 (Book Page): [The selective COX-2 inhibitors do not affect platelet function at their usual doses. The efficacy of COX-2-selective drugs equals that of the older NSAIDs, while GI safety may be improved.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: An RA patient on Methotrexate presents with mucosal ulcers and nausea; what is the corrective management?
back:
• Administer Leucovorin (24 hours after dose)
• Or supplement with daily Folic Acid
• These reduce GI and hematologic toxicity.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): [The incidence of GI and liver function test abnormalities can be reduced by the use of leucovorin 24 hours after each weekly dose or by the use of folic acid.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Describe the metabolic activation of Sulfasalazine and its specific active moiety for RA.
back:
• Split by intestinal bacteria into Sulfapyridine and 5-aminosalicylic acid
• Sulfapyridine: The active moiety for Rheumatoid Arthritis.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): [Sulfasalazine, a csDMARD, is metabolized to sulfapyridine and 5-aminosalicylic acid. The sulfapyridine is probably the active moiety when treating RA.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Q: Classify Tofacitinib within the RA pharmacological framework.
back:
• Targeted synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD)
• Mechanism: Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor
• Interrupts the JAK-STAT signaling pathway
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): [Tofacitinib, though marketed as a biologic, is actually a targeted synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD).] Page 656 (Book Page): [Tofacitinib is a targeted synthetic small molecule (tsDMARD) that selectively inhibits all members of the Janus kinase (JAK) family.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Classify the four main categories of drugs used to manage Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA).
back: 1. NSAIDs (symptom relief). 2. Corticosteroids (anti-inflammatory/bridge therapy). 3. DMARDs (conventional synthetic and biologic). 4. Targeted synthetic DMARDs (JAK inhibitors).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): [The important group of agents are characterized as disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs) including biologics... and the older NSAIDs.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: What is the primary high-yield mechanism of action for low-dose Methotrexate in RA?
back: Inhibition of AICAR transformylase. This leads to intracellular accumulation of AICAR and extracellular accumulation of adenosine, which acts as a potent anti-inflammatory mediator.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): [Methotrexate’s principal mechanism... relates to inhibition of amino-imidazolecarboxamide ribonucleotide (AICAR) transformylase... converted extracellularly to adenosine, which is a potent inhibitor of inflammation.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Contrast the molecular targets of Etanercept versus Adalimumab in RA treatment.
back: Adalimumab: Human monoclonal antibody binding directly to TNF-alpha. Etanercept: Recombinant fusion protein acting as a decoy receptor for TNF-alpha and lymphotoxin-alpha.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 655 (Book Page): [Etanercept is a recombinant fusion protein... binds TNF-α molecules... Adalimumab is a fully human IgG1 anti-TNF monoclonal antibody.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: A patient fails initial Methotrexate therapy for RA. What is the recommended subsequent pharmacological step?
back: Escalate to combination therapy (adding other csDMARDs) or add a biologic DMARD (bDMARD), usually a TNF-alpha inhibitor like Infliximab or Adalimumab.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 665 (Book Page): [Assuming such damage is found, the appropriate approach would be either a combination of nonbiologic DMARDs... or adding a biologic medication, usually a TNF inhibitor.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Which specific enzyme does the active metabolite of Leflunomide inhibit to arrest cell growth?
back: Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH). Inhibition decreases ribonucleotide synthesis, arresting stimulated T-cells in the G1 phase of the cell cycle.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): [This metabolite inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, leading to a decrease in ribonucleotide synthesis and the arrest of stimulated cells in the G1 phase of cell growth.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: What is the most critical monitoring requirement for patients prescribed Hydroxychloroquine for RA?
back: Annual ophthalmologic monitoring. The drug is extensively sequestered in melanin-containing tissues, primarily the eyes, posing a risk for retinal toxicity.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 650 (Book Page): [They are very extensively tissue-bound, particularly in melanin-containing tissues such as the eyes... ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months is advised.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: Define the mechanism and classification of Tofacitinib in RA therapy.
back: Classification: Targeted synthetic DMARD (tsDMARD). Mechanism: Selectively inhibits Janus Kinase (JAK) enzymes (primarily JAK3/JAK1), interrupting the JAK-STAT signaling pathway for cytokine transcription.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): [Tofacitinib is a targeted synthetic small molecule (tsDMARD) that selectively inhibits... JAK3, and to a lesser extent JAK1, hence interrupting the JAK-STAT signaling pathway.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: A patient with new RA symptoms is started on Prednisone. Why is this termed 'Bridge Therapy'?
back: DMARDs take 2-6 months for clinical effect. Corticosteroids provide immediate anti-inflammatory relief and slow bone erosion while waiting for DMARD efficacy.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 658 (Book Page): [The effects of disease-modifying therapies may take 2 weeks to 6 months... Corticosteroids may be administered... to alleviate painful symptoms and... are capable of slowing the appearance of new bone erosions.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: How does Rituximab reduce inflammation in moderate-to-severe RA?
back: It targets the CD20 marker on B-cells, depleting them via cytotoxicity. This reduces antigen presentation to T-cells and inhibits proinflammatory cytokine secretion.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): [Rituximab is a chimeric monoclonal antibody biologic agent that targets CD20 B lymphocytes... reduces inflammation by decreasing the presentation of antigens to T lymphocytes.]

category: Classify the drugs used in RA (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, DMARDs, biologics, targeted therapies, opioids)
front: What is the mechanism by which Abatacept inhibits T-cell activation?
back: It binds to CD80/86 on antigen-presenting cells (APC), preventing interaction with CD28 on T-cells. This blocks the mandatory co-stimulation (second signal) needed for activation.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): [Abatacept... binds to CD80 and 86, thereby inhibiting the binding to CD28 and preventing the activation of T cells.]

category: Describe key pharmacokinetic aspects of major drug groups
front: What percentage of circulating cortisol is bound to corticosteroid-binding globulin (CBG) under normal conditions?
back:
