citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): This drug is contraindicated in pregnancy. Page 652 (Book Page): This drug is contraindicated in pregnancy.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: A patient requires Infliximab for RA. What mandatory screening precaution must be performed first?
back: The patient must be screened for latent or active tuberculosis due to increased reactivation risk.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): All patients should be screened for latent or active tuberculosis before starting TNF-α–blocking agents.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which metabolic supplement reduces GI and hepatic toxicity during Methotrexate therapy?
back: Folic acid or leucovorin (taken 24 hours after the weekly dose) reduces the incidence of these abnormalities.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): The incidence of GI and liver function test abnormalities can be reduced by the use of leucovorin 24 hours after each weekly dose or by the use of folic acid.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which specific reproductive adverse effect is associated with Sulfasalazine in men?
back: Sulfasalazine causes reversible infertility in men; it does not affect female fertility.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): Reversible infertility occurs in men, but sulfasalazine does not affect fertility in women.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What precaution must be taken when discontinuing long-term glucocorticoid therapy in RA patients?
back: Dosage must be tapered slowly to avoid symptom flare and allow the HPA axis to recover.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 713 (Book Page): If corticosteroid dosage is to be reduced, it should be tapered slowly. It may take 2–12 months for the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis to function acceptably.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Why are TNF-alpha blockers contraindicated in patients with symptomatic heart failure?
back: TNF-alpha blockers can exacerbate heart failure symptoms and worsen the underlying condition.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): In patients with borderline or overt heart failure (HF), TNF-α–blocking agents can exacerbate HF.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which agent can be used to rapidly enhance the clearance of Leflunomide in cases of toxicity?
back: Cholestyramine enhances excretion and increases total clearance by approximately 50%.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): Cholestyramine can enhance leflunomide excretion and increases total clearance by approximately 50%.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What is the most significant catabolic adverse effect of long-term glucocorticoids on connective tissue?
back: Glucocorticoids cause thinning of the skin, muscle wasting, and osteoporosis in bone.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 708 (Book Page): Supraphysiologic amounts of glucocorticoids lead to decreased muscle mass and weakness and thinning of the skin. Catabolic and antianabolic effects on bone are the cause of osteoporosis.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which specific condition strictly contraindicates the use of methotrexate in patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
• Pregnancy
• It is an antimetabolite that causes direct fetal harm.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): [Methotrexate] drug is contraindicated in pregnancy.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: How do NSAIDs physiologically cause nephrotoxicity regarding renal blood flow regulation?
back:
• Interference with renal blood flow autoregulation.
• Mechanism: Inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis which normally modulates flow.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 644 (Book Page): Nephrotoxicity, reported for all NSAIDs, is due, in part, to interference with the autoregulation of renal blood flow, which is modulated by prostaglandins.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which mandatory screening tests must be performed before initiating any TNF-alpha blocking agent for RA?
back:
• Latent Tuberculosis (TB) screening.
• Viral Hepatitis (specifically Hepatitis B) screening.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): All patients should be screened for latent or active tuberculosis before starting TNF-α–blocking agents. The use of TNF-α–blocking agents is also associated with increased risk of HBV reactivation.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: An RA patient on tocilizumab with a history of diverticulitis presents with sudden abdominal pain. What complication is suspected?
back:
• Gastrointestinal (GI) perforation.
• Risk is increased in patients with diverticulitis or concurrent corticosteroid use.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): GI perforation has been reported when using tocilizumab in patients with diverticulitis and in those using corticosteroids.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which pharmacological intervention is used to rapidly accelerate the elimination of leflunomide's active metabolite?
back:
• Cholestyramine administration.
• It increases total drug clearance by approximately 50%.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): Cholestyramine can enhance leflunomide excretion and increases total clearance by approximately 50%.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What is the primary organ-specific toxicity associated with hydroxychloroquine that requires annual specialist monitoring?
back:
• Ocular (Retinal) toxicity.
• Requirement: Specialist ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 650 (Book Page): Although ocular toxicity (see Chapter 52) may occur... ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months is advised.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which medications should be administered 30 minutes prior to a rituximab infusion to reduce adverse reactions?
back:
• Acetaminophen.
• Antihistamines.
• Intravenous methylprednisolone (glucocorticoid).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): Pretreatment with acetaminophen, an antihistamine, and intravenous glucocorticoids (usually 100 mg of methylprednisolone) given 30 minutes prior to infusion decreases the incidence and severity of infusion reactions.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: A male RA patient on sulfasalazine reports difficulty conceiving. What is the most likely drug-induced cause?
back:
• Reversible male infertility.
• Note: Sulfasalazine affects male fertility but typically does not affect female fertility.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): Reversible infertility occurs in men, but sulfasalazine does not affect fertility in women.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which metabolic parameters must be monitored periodically in RA patients starting the JAK inhibitor tofacitinib?
back:
• Lipid levels (Total Cholesterol, LDL, and HDL).
• Elevation typically begins about 6 weeks after starting treatment.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): Dose-dependent increases in the levels of low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and total cholesterol have been found... lipid levels should be monitored.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What is the most common local adverse effect reported by patients receiving subcutaneous anakinra injections?
back:
• Injection site reactions.
• These occur in up to 40% of patients.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 658 (Book Page): The most common adverse effects are injection site reactions (up to 40%).

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which periodic laboratory evaluation is essential for detecting dose-related hepatotoxicity in RA patients on Methotrexate?
back: Monitoring of liver enzymes (LFTs). While cirrhosis occurs in <1% of patients, progressive dose-related enzyme elevations are common.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): Progressive dose-related hepatotoxicity in the form of enzyme elevation occurs frequently, but cirrhosis is rare (<1%).

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What is the primary toxicity precaution for RA patients receiving Hydroxychloroquine doses exceeding 6.4 mg/kg/d?
back: Annual ophthalmologic monitoring for retinal toxicity. The drug is extensively tissue-bound, particularly in melanin-containing structures like the eyes.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 650 (Book Page): ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months is advised... ocular toxicity (see Chapter 52) may occur at dosages greater than 250 mg/d for chloroquine and greater than 6.4 mg/kg/d for hydroxychloroquine.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which reversible reproductive side effect should male patients be cautioned about when starting Sulfasalazine for RA?
back: Reversible infertility. Notably, it does not affect female fertility and is generally not considered teratogenic.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): Reversible infertility occurs in men, but sulfasalazine does not affect fertility in women. The drug does not appear to be teratogenic.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Patients beginning Infliximab or other TNF-alpha blockers must be screened for which two latent infections?
back:
1. Latent Tuberculosis (TB): Risk of activation.
2. Hepatitis B Virus (HBV): Risk of reactivation.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): all patients should be screened for latent or active tuberculosis before starting TNF-α–blocking agents... associated with increased risk of HBV reactivation.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Besides liver enzymes, which biochemical parameters require monitoring in RA patients treated with the IL-6 inhibitor Tocilizumab?
back: Lipid profile (Cholesterol, Triglycerides, LDL, HDL). Tocilizumab may also cause neutropenia and thrombocytopenia.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): lipids (eg, cholesterol, triglycerides, LDL, and HDL) should be monitored... common adverse reactions are upper respiratory tract infections, headache, hypertension, and elevated liver enzymes.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What rare malignancy requires long-term vigilance even five years after stopping chronic Cyclophosphamide therapy for RA?
back: Bladder cancer. Monitoring for hematuria and cytological changes is necessary due to the drug's metabolic profile.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): Bladder cancer is very rare but must be looked for, even 5 years after cessation of use.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: At what time interval should lipid levels be assessed after initiating Tofacitinib for moderate-to-severe RA?
back: Approximately 6 weeks. Tofacitinib causes dose-dependent increases in LDL, HDL, and total cholesterol within this timeframe.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): Dose-dependent increases in the levels of low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and total cholesterol have been found in patients receiving tofacitinib, often beginning about 6 weeks after starting treatment.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Why is concurrent Ibuprofen administration a precaution in RA patients taking low-dose Aspirin for cardioprotection?
back: Ibuprofen antagonizes the irreversible platelet inhibition of Aspirin, potentially reducing its effectiveness in preventing cardiovascular events.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 648 (Book Page): The concomitant administration of ibuprofen and aspirin antagonizes the irreversible platelet inhibition induced by aspirin.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which infectious precaution is mandatory before starting chronic high-dose Prednisone therapy for RA flares?
back: Tuberculin testing and chest X-rays. Glucocorticoids can reactivate dormant tuberculosis by suppressing the host immune response.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 711 (Book Page): obtain chest x-rays and a tuberculin test, since glucocorticoid therapy can reactivate dormant tuberculosis.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: In which specific patient population are TNF-alpha blocking agents (e.g., Adalimumab) generally contraindicated or used with caution?
back: Patients with Heart Failure (HF). These agents can exacerbate symptoms and worsen outcomes in borderline or overt HF.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): In patients with borderline or overt heart failure (HF), TNF-α–blocking agents can exacerbate HF.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What is the specific FDA "black box" warning associated with Celecoxib in RA treatment?
back: Cardiovascular risks, specifically increased risk of myocardial infarction (MI) and stroke.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 644 (Book Page): [Celecoxib has a U.S Food and Drug Administration (FDA) “black box” warning concerning cardiovascular risks.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Why is aspirin therapy strictly contraindicated in patients with hemophilia?
back: Irreversible inhibition of platelet cyclooxygenase (COX) impairs aggregation for the platelet's lifespan (8–10 days), increasing bleeding risk.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 645 (Book Page): [The antiplatelet action of aspirin contraindicates its use by patients with hemophilia.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which viral screening is mandatory before initiating Rituximab for rheumatoid arthritis?
back: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV). Rituximab is associated with potentially fatal HBV reactivation.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): [Rituximab is associated with reactivation of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, which requires monitoring before and several months after the initiation of the treatment.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What rare, acute respiratory toxicity is associated with Methotrexate therapy?
back: Hypersensitivity-like lung reaction manifesting as acute shortness of breath.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): [A rare hypersensitivity-like lung reaction with acute shortness of breath has been documented...]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Why must TNF-α inhibitors (e.g., Infliximab) be avoided in patients with borderline heart failure?
back: These agents can exacerbate borderline or overt heart failure (HF).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): [In patients with borderline or overt heart failure (HF), TNF-α–blocking agents can exacerbate HF.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Describe the gender-specific side effect of Sulfasalazine used in RA.
back: Reversible infertility in men; it does not affect female fertility.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): [Reversible infertility occurs in men, but sulfasalazine does not affect fertility in women.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Why is co-administration of Abatacept with other biologics like TNF antagonists restricted?
back: It significantly increases the incidence of serious infections without increasing therapeutic efficacy.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 650 (Book Page): [Concomitant use with TNF-α antagonists or other biologics is not recommended due to the increased incidence of serious infection.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which ophthalmic condition requires periodic slit-lamp screening in patients on long-term corticosteroids?
back: Posterior subcapsular cataracts.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 713 (Book Page): [Long-term therapy with intermediate- and long-acting steroids is associated with... the development of posterior subcapsular cataracts.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What metabolic parameter must be monitored 6 weeks after starting the JAK inhibitor Tofacitinib?
back: Lipid levels (Cholesterol, LDL, HDL) due to dose-dependent increases.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): [Dose-dependent increases in the levels of low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and total cholesterol... lipid levels should be monitored.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: At what hydrocortisone dosage does pediatric growth retardation become a risk in chronic therapy?
back: Dosages exceeding 45 mg/m² per day.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 713 (Book Page): [In dosages of 45 mg/m² per day or more of hydrocortisone or its equivalent, growth retardation occurs in children.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What are the two most frequent toxicities associated with low-dose methotrexate therapy in RA?
back:
- Nausea
- Mucosal ulcers (stomatitis)
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): Nausea and mucosal ulcers are the most common toxicities.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Why is Leflunomide strictly contraindicated during pregnancy based on its cellular mechanism?
back:
- Inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase
- Decreases ribonucleotide synthesis
- Arrests cell growth in G1 phase (teratogenic)
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): This metabolite inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, leading to a decrease in ribonucleotide synthesis and the arrest of stimulated cells in the G1 phase of cell growth... This drug is contraindicated in pregnancy.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: How does the risk of latent tuberculosis activation differ between Etanercept and other TNF-α blockers?
back:
- Risk is lower with Etanercept than with other TNF-α blocking agents.
- Screening is mandatory for all TNF-α inhibitors.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): Activation of latent tuberculosis is lower with etanercept than with other TNF-α–blocking agents. Nevertheless, all patients should be screened for latent or active tuberculosis before starting TNF-α–blocking agents.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: A patient starting Azathioprine develops severe myelosuppression. Which genetic deficiency most likely caused this toxicity?
back:
- Thiopurine methyltransferase (TPMT) deficiency
- Causes toxic accumulation of 6-thioguanine
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 650 (Book Page): Production of 6-thioguanine is dependent on thiopurine methyltransferase (TPMT), and patients with low or absent TPMT activity... are at particularly high risk of myelosuppression.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which metabolic component of Sulfasalazine is active in RA, and what are its common adverse effects?
back:
- Active moiety: Sulfapyridine
- Adverse effects: Nausea, vomiting, headache, and rash
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): The sulfapyridine is probably the active moiety when treating RA... Common adverse effects include nausea, vomiting, headache, and rash.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What specific long-term monitoring is required for patients on Hydroxychloroquine to prevent irreversible toxicity?
back:
- Ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months
- Used to detect retinal/ocular toxicity
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 650 (Book Page): Although ocular toxicity... rarely occurs at lower doses. Nevertheless, ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months is advised.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What metabolic parameter must be monitored regularly in RA patients receiving the JAK inhibitor Tofacitinib?
back:
- Lipid levels (LDL, HDL, and total cholesterol)
- Increases occur within 6 weeks of starting therapy
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): Dose-dependent increases in the levels of low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and total cholesterol have been found in patients receiving tofacitinib... therefore, lipid levels should be monitored.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which class of NSAIDs is preferred for RA patients with renal insufficiency and why?
back:
- Nonacetylated salicylates (e.g., Salsalate)
- They lack potent prostaglandin inhibition and do not inhibit platelet aggregation.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 649 (Book Page): For patients with renal insufficiency, nonacetylated salicylates may be best. Page 645 (Book Page): nonacetylated salicylates... do not inhibit platelet aggregation.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What viral screening is mandatory before initiating Rituximab therapy in RA patients?
back:
- Hepatitis B virus (HBV) screening
- Associated with serious reactivation risk
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): Rituximab is associated with reactivation of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, which requires monitoring before and several months after the initiation of the treatment.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What is the primary catabolic bone toxicity associated with long-term glucocorticoid use in RA?
back:
- Osteoporosis
- Limits long-term therapeutic utility
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 708 (Book Page): Catabolic and antianabolic effects on bone are the cause of osteoporosis... and impose a major limitation in the long-term therapeutic use of glucocorticoids.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What are the primary dose-related toxicities associated with low-dose Methotrexate therapy in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
• Nausea and mucosal ulcers (stomatitis)
• Dose-related hepatotoxicity (enzyme elevation)
• Bone marrow suppression (leukopenia/anemia)
• Rare hypersensitivity-like lung reactions
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): Nausea and mucosal ulcers are the most common toxicities... leukopenia, anemia, stomatitis, GI ulcerations... hepatotoxicity... cirrhosis is rare.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Describe the characteristic clinical features of iatrogenic Cushing’s syndrome resulting from chronic glucocorticoid use.
back:
• Moon facies and truncal fat redistribution
• Muscle wasting and significant protein loss
• Skin thinning, purple striae, and easy bruising
• Osteoporosis and impaired wound healing
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 712 (Book Page): iatrogenic Cushing’s syndrome... muscle wasting; thinning, purple striae, and easy bruising of the skin; poor wound healing; and osteoporosis.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What is a major clinical contraindication and a common gastrointestinal adverse effect of Leflunomide therapy?
back:
• Contraindication: Pregnancy (teratogenic effects)
• Adverse Effect: Diarrhea (occurs in ~25% of patients)
• Other effects include mild alopecia and weight gain
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): Diarrhea occurs in approximately 25% of patients... This drug is contraindicated in pregnancy.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which infectious screenings are mandatory before initiating TNF-alpha blocking agents like Infliximab or Adalimumab?
back:
• Latent Tuberculosis (TB skin or blood test)
• Viral Hepatitis B (HBV) serology
• Reason: High risk of reactivation due to immunosuppression
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): All patients should be screened for latent or active tuberculosis before starting TNF-α–blocking agents... also associated with increased risk of HBV reactivation.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which specific organ toxicity requires annual ophthalmologic monitoring for patients on long-term Hydroxychloroquine?
back:
• Ocular toxicity (retinal damage)
• Monitoring: Examination every 12 months
• Risk increases at dosages >6.4 mg/kg/day
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 650 (Book Page): Although ocular toxicity... may occur... ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months is advised.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Identify the most common adverse effects and the reversible reproductive concern for males taking Sulfasalazine.
back:
• Adverse effects: Nausea, vomiting, and headache
• Reproductive concern: Reversible infertility (decreased sperm count)
• Note: It is not considered teratogenic
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): Common adverse effects include nausea, vomiting, headache, and rash... Reversible infertility occurs in men.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What precautions are necessary to prevent infusion reactions and manage viral risks with Rituximab therapy?
back:
• Pretreatment: Acetaminophen, antihistamines, and Glucocorticoids (30 mins prior)
• Monitoring: Screen for Hepatitis B (HBV) reactivation
• Periodic blood counts for cytopenias
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): Pretreatment with acetaminophen, an antihistamine, and intravenous glucocorticoids... Rituximab is associated with reactivation of hepatitis B.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Explain why Infliximab is typically co-administered with Methotrexate in RA patients.
back:
• Methotrexate reduces the development of Human Antichimeric Antibodies (HACA)
• Prevents loss of drug efficacy over time
• Decreases the risk of infusion-related reactions
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 669 (Book Page): Infliximab elicits human antichimeric antibodies... Concurrent therapy with methotrexate markedly decreases the prevalence.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: List the laboratory monitoring requirements for patients receiving the IL-6 inhibitor Tocilizumab.
back:
• Liver function tests (risk of elevated enzymes)
• Complete blood count (risk of neutropenia/thrombocytopenia)
• Lipid profile (cholesterol and triglycerides)
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): The most common adverse reactions are... elevated liver enzymes. Neutropenia and reduction in platelet counts occur... lipids... should be monitored.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What are the significant long-term toxicities of Cyclophosphamide therapy in severe rheumatic diseases?
back:
• Permanent sterility (especially in women)
• Risk of Bladder Cancer (hemorrhagic cystitis)
• Myelosuppression (leukopenia/thrombocytopenia)
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): sterility may occur after chronic dosing... especially in women. Bladder cancer is very rare but must be looked for.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What are the primary dose-related toxicities of Methotrexate in RA treatment?
back:
• Mucosal ulcers and stomatitis
• Bone marrow suppression (leukopenia, anemia)
• Dose-related hepatotoxicity (enzyme elevation)
• Rare hypersensitivity lung reactions
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): [Nausea and mucosal ulcers are the most common toxicities. Additionally, many other side effects such as leukopenia, anemia, stomatitis... Progressive dose-related hepatotoxicity in the form of enzyme elevation occurs frequently]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Why is Leflunomide strictly contraindicated in female patients of childbearing age?
back:
• Highly teratogenic (Pregnancy Category X)
• Long half-life (19 days) requires cholestyramine washout before conception
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): [leflunomide inhibits T-cell proliferation and reduces production of autoantibodies... This drug is contraindicated in pregnancy... mean plasma half-life of 19 days... Cholestyramine can enhance leflunomide excretion]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What specific organ toxicity requires annual screening for patients on Hydroxychloroquine?
back:
• Ocular toxicity (retinopathy)
• Risk increases at dosages >6.4 mg/kg/day
• Requires ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 650 (Book Page): [ocular toxicity... may occur at dosages greater than 250 mg/d for chloroquine and greater than 6.4 mg/kg/d for hydroxychloroquine... ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months is advised.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which mandatory screenings must be performed before starting TNF-α inhibitors like Infliximab?
back:
• Latent or active Tuberculosis (TB) screening
• Hepatitis B virus (HBV) screening
• Prevents reactivation of latent infections
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): [all patients should be screened for latent or active tuberculosis before starting TNF-α–blocking agents... also associated with increased risk of HBV reactivation; screening for HBV is important before starting the treatment.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What are the major musculoskeletal toxicities of long-term Glucocorticoid use in RA?
back:
• Osteoporosis and pathological fractures
• Aseptic (avascular) necrosis of the hip
• Steroid myopathy and muscle wasting
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 712 (Book Page): [Catabolic and antianabolic effects on bone are the cause of osteoporosis... eventually osteoporosis, diabetes, and aseptic necrosis of the hip... myopathy and muscle wasting]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What is the mechanism of NSAID-induced acute renal insufficiency?
back:
• Inhibition of vasodilatory prostaglandins (PGE2, PGI2)
• Disrupts compensatory renal blood flow autoregulation
• Leads to decreased glomerular filtration rate (GFR)
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 644 (Book Page): [Nephrotoxicity, reported for all NSAIDs, is due, in part, to interference with the autoregulation of renal blood flow, which is modulated by prostaglandins.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What specific reversible side effect occurs in men using Sulfasalazine for RA?
back:
• Reversible infertility (reduced sperm count/motility)
• Does not affect female fertility or cause teratogenicity
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): [Reversible infertility occurs in men, but sulfasalazine does not affect fertility in women. The drug does not appear to be teratogenic.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which metabolic parameter requires monitoring during Tofacitinib therapy?
back:
• Lipid profiles (LDL, HDL, and total cholesterol)
• Levels typically increase 6 weeks after starting treatment
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): [Dose-dependent increases in the levels of low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and total cholesterol have been found... lipid levels should be monitored.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What infectious risk is specifically associated with Rituximab therapy?
back:
• Reactivation of Hepatitis B virus (HBV)
• Increased risk of fatal bacterial, fungal, and viral infections
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): [Rituximab is associated with reactivation of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection... Serious, and sometimes fatal, bacterial, fungal, and viral infections are reported]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Tocilizumab is associated with an increased risk of perforation in which GI condition?
back:
• Diverticulitis
• Risk is higher when used concurrently with systemic corticosteroids
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): [GI perforation has been reported when using tocilizumab in patients with diverticulitis and in those using corticosteroids]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: What is the primary absolute contraindication for Leflunomide in the treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: Pregnancy (the drug is highly teratogenic).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): This drug is contraindicated in pregnancy.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Which supplement reduces the incidence of gastrointestinal and hepatic toxicities in patients on Methotrexate?
back: Folic acid (or leucovorin).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): The incidence of GI and liver function test abnormalities can be reduced by the use of leucovorin 24 hours after each weekly dose or by the use of folic acid

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Why must Celecoxib be used with caution in patients with a history of sulfonamide (sulfa) allergy?
back: Celecoxib contains a sulfonamide moiety that may trigger allergic rashes.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 647 (Book Page): Probably because it is a sulfonamide, celecoxib may cause rashes.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Before initiating TNF-alpha inhibitors like Infliximab, which two specific latent infections must be screened for?
back:
1. Tuberculosis (TB)
2. Hepatitis B Virus (HBV)
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): all patients should be screened for latent or active tuberculosis... increased risk of HBV reactivation; screening for HBV is important before starting the treatment.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: What is the clinical rationale for slowly tapering glucocorticoids rather than abrupt cessation after long-term use?
back: To prevent acute adrenal insufficiency (adrenal crisis) caused by HPA axis suppression.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 713 (Book Page): When corticosteroids are administered for more than 2 weeks, adrenal suppression may occur... If corticosteroid dosage is to be reduced, it should be tapered slowly.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Which specific toxicity necessitates an annual ophthalmologic examination for patients on Hydroxychloroquine?
back: Ocular toxicity (specifically retinal damage/retinopathy).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 650 (Book Page): although ocular toxicity (see Chapter 52) may occur... ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months is advised.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: What unique, reversible reproductive side effect occurs in male patients taking Sulfasalazine?
back: Infertility (specifically reversible male infertility).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): Reversible infertility occurs in men, but sulfasalazine does not affect fertility in women.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: In patients with comorbid Rheumatoid Arthritis and borderline Heart Failure, which class of DMARDs can exacerbate the cardiac condition?
back: TNF-alpha blocking agents (e.g., Infliximab, Adalimumab, Etanercept).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): In patients with borderline or overt heart failure (HF), TNF-α–blocking agents can exacerbate HF.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Which severe gastrointestinal complication is a reported risk for patients taking IL-6 inhibitors like Tocilizumab?
back: Gastrointestinal (GI) perforation (especially in patients with diverticulitis or using corticosteroids).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): GI perforation has been reported when using tocilizumab in patients with diverticulitis and in those using corticosteroids

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Approximately what percentage of patients discontinue Sulfasalazine due to toxicity-related side effects?
back: 30% of patients.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): Approximately 30% of patients using sulfasalazine discontinue the drug because of toxicity.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which adverse effects are most characteristic of low-dose methotrexate therapy in RA?
back:
• Nausea and mucosal ulcers.
• Potential hepatotoxicity (enzyme elevation).
• Bone marrow suppression (leukopenia, anemia).
• Hypersensitivity-like lung reactions.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): Nausea and mucosal ulcers are the most common toxicities. Additionally, many other side effects such as leukopenia, anemia, stomatitis, GI ulcerations, and alopecia are probably the result of inhibiting cellular proliferation.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What is the primary catabolic concern for long-term glucocorticoid use in bone tissue?
back:
• Induction of osteoporosis.
• Antagonism of vitamin D-mediated calcium absorption.
• Increased risk of aseptic necrosis (especially the hip).
• Major limitation for chronic therapeutic use.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 708 (Book Page): Catabolic and antianabolic effects on bone are the cause of osteoporosis in Cushing’s syndrome and impose a major limitation in the long-term therapeutic use of glucocorticoids.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What specific monitoring is mandatory for patients on long-term hydroxychloroquine therapy?
back:
• Ophthalmologic monitoring for retinal toxicity.
• Recommended screening frequency is every 12 months.
• Risk increases at dosages exceeding 6.4 mg/kg/day.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 650 (Book Page): ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months is advised. ... Although ocular toxicity ... may occur at dosages greater than ... 6.4 mg/kg/d for hydroxychloroquine, it rarely occurs at lower doses.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Why are TNF-alpha blocking agents generally avoided or used with extreme caution in heart failure patients?
back:
• Potential to exacerbate borderline or overt heart failure.
• Associated with worsening of cardiac function.
• Requires baseline and periodic cardiovascular assessment.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): In patients with borderline or overt heart failure (HF), TNF-α–blocking agents can exacerbate HF.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which genetic deficiency predisposes patients to severe myelosuppression when taking azathioprine?
back:
• Thiopurine methyltransferase (TPMT) deficiency.
• Leads to accumulation of excess parent drug concentrations.
• Results in life-threatening bone marrow suppression.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 650 (Book Page): Production of 6-thioguanine is dependent on thiopurine methyltransferase (TPMT), and patients with low or absent TPMT activity ... are at particularly high risk of myelosuppression.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What is the primary absolute contraindication for the use of leflunomide in RA?
back:
• Pregnancy (highly teratogenic).
• Severe hepatic impairment.
• Known hypersensitivity to the drug.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): This drug is contraindicated in pregnancy. ... Elevation in liver enzymes can occur.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Why must glucocorticoids be tapered slowly after therapy exceeding two weeks?
back:
• To prevent acute adrenal insufficiency.
• Allows time for HPA axis recovery (may take 2–12 months).
• Prevents withdrawal syndrome (fever, myalgia, arthralgia).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 713 (Book Page): When corticosteroids are administered for more than 2 weeks, adrenal suppression may occur. ... If corticosteroid dosage is to be reduced, it should be tapered slowly.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which specific gastrointestinal toxicity is associated with the IL-6 receptor antagonist tocilizumab?
back:
• Gastrointestinal perforation.
• Increased risk in patients with history of diverticulitis.
• Concomitant corticosteroid use further increases risk.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): GI perforation has been reported when using tocilizumab in patients with diverticulitis and in those using corticosteroids.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What is the pathophysiological mechanism behind NSAID-induced nephrotoxicity?
back:
• Interference with renal blood flow autoregulation.
• Inhibition of prostaglandin-mediated vasodilation.
• Can lead to renal insufficiency, hyperkalemia, and failure.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 644 (Book Page): Nephrotoxicity, reported for all NSAIDs, is due, in part, to interference with the autoregulation of renal blood flow, which is modulated by prostaglandins.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What unique, reversible side effect is associated with sulfasalazine use in male RA patients?
back:
• Reversible infertility (sperm count/motility effects).
• Does not typically affect female fertility.
• Generally resolves upon drug discontinuation.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): Reversible infertility occurs in men, but sulfasalazine does not affect fertility in women. The drug does not appear to be teratogenic.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What are the most common high-yield toxicities of low-dose Methotrexate in RA therapy?
back:
- Nausea and mucosal ulcerations.
- Bone marrow suppression (leukopenia, anemia).
- Dose-related hepatotoxicity (enzyme elevation).
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): [Nausea and mucosal ulcers are the most common toxicities. Additionally, many other side effects such as leukopenia, anemia, stomatitis, GI ulcerations... Progressive dose-related hepatotoxicity in the form of enzyme elevation occurs frequently.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What is the physiological mechanism behind NSAID-induced nephrotoxicity in RA patients?
back:
- Inhibition of renal prostaglandin synthesis.
- Disruption of the autoregulation of renal blood flow.
- Leads to fluid retention, hypertension, and hyperkalemia.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 659 (Book Page): [Nephrotoxicity, reported for all NSAIDs, is due, in part, to interference with the autoregulation of renal blood flow, which is modulated by prostaglandins.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: How does Celecoxib differ from non-selective NSAIDs regarding gastrointestinal and platelet safety?
back:
- Improved GI safety with fewer endoscopic ulcers.
- No impact on platelet aggregation at therapeutic doses.
- Spares COX-1 'housekeeping' isozymes in the gut and platelets.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 660 (Book Page): [The selective COX-2 inhibitors do not affect platelet function at their usual doses. The efficacy of COX-2-selective drugs equals that of the older NSAIDs, while GI safety may be improved.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which mandatory screening protocol must be completed before starting TNF-alpha blocking agents?
back:
- Screening for latent or active Tuberculosis (PPD or IGRA).
- Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) screening due to risk of reactivation.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 656 (Book Page): [All patients should be screened for latent or active tuberculosis before starting TNF-alpha blocking agents. The use of TNF-alpha blocking agents is also associated with increased risk of HBV reactivation.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What unique, reversible adverse effect is associated with Sulfasalazine use in male RA patients?
back:
- Reversible infertility (decreased sperm count/motility).
- Note: Fertility in women remains unaffected by the drug.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): [Reversible infertility occurs in men, but sulfasalazine does not affect fertility in women.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which specific Hydroxychloroquine toxicity requires ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months?
back:
- Ocular toxicity (retinopathy).
- Results from drug binding to melanin-containing tissues in the eye.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 650 (Book Page): [ocular toxicity... rarely occurs at lower doses. Nevertheless, ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months is advised... Antimalarials... are very extensively tissue-bound, particularly in melanin-containing tissues such as the eyes.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What metabolic disturbance requires routine monitoring during Tofacitinib therapy in RA?
back:
- Elevation of serum lipids (LDL, HDL, and total cholesterol).
- Usually increases approximately 6 weeks after starting treatment.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): [Dose-dependent increases in the levels of low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and total cholesterol have been found in patients receiving tofacitinib... therefore, lipid levels should be monitored.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Why is abrupt discontinuation of long-term glucocorticoids contraindicated in RA management?
back:
- Risk of iatrogenic adrenal crisis/insufficiency.
- HPA axis may require 2-12 months for recovery after suppression.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 713 (Book Page): [If corticosteroid dosage is to be reduced, it should be tapered slowly... It may take 2–12 months for the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis to function acceptably.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: How can the total clearance of Leflunomide be enhanced by approximately 50% in case of toxicity?
back:
- Administration of Cholestyramine.
- Enhances excretion by disrupting enterohepatic recirculation.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): [Cholestyramine can enhance leflunomide excretion and increases total clearance by approximately 50%.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which viral reactivation risk is specific to the B-cell depleting biologic Rituximab?
back:
- Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) reactivation.
- Monitoring is required before and several months after initiating therapy.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): [Rituximab is associated with reactivation of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, which requires monitoring before and several months after the initiation of the treatment.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: What are the two most common mucosal and gastrointestinal toxicities associated with methotrexate therapy?
back: - Nausea - Mucosal ulcers - These effects result from inhibition of cellular proliferation and can be minimized with folic acid supplementation.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 666 (Book Page): Nausea and mucosal ulcers are the most common toxicities. Additionally, many other side effects... are probably the result of inhibiting cellular proliferation.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Explain the pathophysiological mechanism behind leflunomide-induced diarrhea seen in approximately twenty-five percent of patients.
back: - Inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase - Arrests stimulated cells in the G1 phase - Directly impacts rapidly dividing intestinal mucosal cells.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 665 (Book Page): This metabolite inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase... inhibits T-cell proliferation... Diarrhea occurs in approximately 25% of patients

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Contrast the cardiovascular risks of selective COX-2 inhibitors compared to standard non-selective NSAID medications.
back: - Selective COX-2 inhibitors (e.g., Celecoxib) increase risks of edema and hypertension - Associated with higher myocardial infarction rates than naproxen.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 658 (Book Page): selective COX-2 inhibitors increase the incidence of edema, hypertension, and possibly, myocardial infarction.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Why are TNF-alpha blocking agents strictly contraindicated in patients with borderline or overt heart failure?
back: - TNF-alpha is required for cardiac homeostasis - Antagonists can exacerbate heart failure symptoms and significantly increase mortality risk.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 670 (Book Page): In patients with borderline or overt heart failure (HF), TNF-alpha–blocking agents can exacerbate HF.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Which specific screening is mandatory for patients on long-term hydroxychloroquine to prevent irreversible drug-induced toxicity?
back: - Annual ophthalmologic or retinal examination - Rationale: The drug binds extensively to melanin-containing tissues in the eye, causing potential toxicity.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 664 (Book Page): ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months is advised... extensively tissue-bound, particularly in melanin-containing tissues such as the eyes.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Identify the primary bone-related toxicity that limits long-term therapeutic use of glucocorticoids in rheumatoid arthritis.
back: - Osteoporosis - Rationale: Glucocorticoids exert catabolic and antianabolic effects on bone, leading to increased fracture risk.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 722 (Book Page): Catabolic and antianabolic effects on bone are the cause of osteoporosis... and impose a major limitation in the long-term therapeutic use of glucocorticoids.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: What precaution regarding immunization must be followed for patients currently receiving abatacept therapy for RA?
back: - Avoid live vaccines during and for three months after therapy - Rationale: Abatacept suppresses T-cell activation, increasing infection risk from vaccines.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 664 (Book Page): Live vaccines should be avoided in patients while taking abatacept and up to 3 months after discontinuation.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Which life-threatening viral reactivation risk must be screened for before initiating rituximab therapy in RA?
back: - Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation - Rationale: CD20 B-cell depletion can trigger lethal reactivation of latent HBV in positive patients.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 666 (Book Page): Rituximab is associated with reactivation of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, which requires monitoring before and several months after the initiation

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Describe the physical fat redistribution pattern characteristic of iatrogenic Cushing’s syndrome caused by chronic glucocorticoids.
back: - Moon facies (face rounding) - Buffalo hump (fat on back of neck) - Visceral and supraclavicular fat deposition with truncal obesity.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 726 (Book Page): rounding, puffiness, fat deposition, and plethora usually appear (moon facies)... fat tends to be redistributed from the extremities to the trunk, the back of the neck, and the supraclavicular fossae.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Name the first-line DMARD that is strictly contraindicated in pregnancy due to its potent teratogenic antimetabolite effects.
back: - Methotrexate - Mechanism: It inhibits DNA synthesis and cellular proliferation, making it strictly contraindicated for all pregnant women.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 666 (Book Page): This drug [Methotrexate] is contraindicated in pregnancy.

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What are the two most common toxicities associated with the use of Methotrexate in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: 1. Nausea and mucosal ulcers (stomatitis) 2. Dose-related hepatotoxicity through enzyme elevation 3. Side effects generally result from inhibited cellular proliferation.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 666 (Book Page): "Nausea and mucosal ulcers are the most common toxicities. Additionally, many other side effects... are probably the result of inhibiting cellular proliferation."

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What specific mechanism explains the nephrotoxicity associated with the administration of all nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs?
back: 1. Interference with the autoregulation of renal blood flow 2. Result of prostaglandin biosynthesis inhibition 3. Potentially leads to renal insufficiency or acute failure.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 659 (Book Page): "Nephrotoxicity, reported for all NSAIDs, is due, in part, to interference with the autoregulation of renal blood flow, which is modulated by prostaglandins."

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
coreConcept: Selective vs Nonselective NSAID GI Safety
front: Q: How does the gastrointestinal safety profile of Celecoxib contrast with nonselective NSAIDs like Piroxicam?
back: 1. Celecoxib causes fewer endoscopic ulcers by sparing COX-1 2. Piroxicam (especially >20mg/d) carries a significantly higher risk of peptic ulcers and bleeding.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 662 (Book Page): "Celecoxib is associated with fewer endoscopic ulcers than most other NSAIDs. ...piroxicam is used in dosages higher than 20 mg/d, an increased incidence of peptic ulcer and bleeding... is encountered."

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What mandatory screenings must be performed before initiating any TNF-alpha blocking agent in a Rheumatoid Arthritis patient?
back: 1. Screen for latent or active tuberculosis (TB) 2. Screen for Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation risk 3. Necessary to prevent reactivation of macrophage-dependent infections.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 670 (Book Page): "Screening for tuberculosis should be done prior to beginning... TNF-α–blocking agents... also associated with increased risk of HBV reactivation."

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What pharmacological step accelerates the elimination of Leflunomide's active metabolite in cases of toxicity or planned pregnancy?
back: 1. Administration of Cholestyramine 2. Enhances the excretion of the A77-1726 metabolite 3. Increases total clearance by approximately 50% to counteract the 19-day half-life.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 666 (Book Page): "Cholestyramine can enhance leflunomide excretion and increases total clearance by approximately 50%."

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which clinical monitoring procedure is mandatory every 12 months for patients prescribed Hydroxychloroquine for Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: 1. Annual ophthalmologic monitoring (eye examination) 2. Screen for dose-related ocular/retinal toxicity 3. Essential for dosages exceeding 6.4 mg/kg/d.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 665 (Book Page): "Although ocular toxicity... may occur... ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months is advised."

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which metabolic parameters must be strictly monitored in patients receiving the Janus kinase inhibitor Tofacitinib for RA?
back: 1. Lipid profiles including LDL, HDL, and total cholesterol 2. Monitoring begins at 6 weeks following drug initiation 3. Required due to potential additive cardiovascular event risks.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 672 (Book Page): "Dose-dependent increases in the levels of low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and total cholesterol have been found in patients receiving tofacitinib."

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: A patient on high-dose Prednisone presents with proximal muscle weakness and thinning skin; how is this clinically identified?
back: 1. Differentiated as Iatrogenic Cushing's Syndrome 2. Clinical hallmarks include steroid-induced proximal myopathy 3. Distinguished from RA by presence of moon facies and visceral fat deposition.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 727 (Book Page): "iatrogenic Cushing’s syndrome. ...over time result in weight gain; visceral fat deposition; myopathy and muscle wasting; thinning of the skin."

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Describe the physiological consequence of inhibiting Interleukin-6 with Tocilizumab regarding the cytochrome P450 enzyme system.
back: 1. Inhibiting IL-6 restores CYP450 activity to higher levels 2. Restores enzymes previously suppressed by cytokine-mediated signaling 3. Requires dosage adjustment for substrates with narrow therapeutic windows.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 668 (Book Page): "IL-6 can suppress several CYP450 isoenzymes; thus, inhibiting IL-6 may restore CYP450 activities to higher levels."

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What reversible reproductive side effect is specifically associated with the use of Sulfasalazine in male patients?
back: 1. Reversible infertility 2. Does not affect fertility in women or show teratogenicity 3. Occurs in approximately 30% of patients who discontinue the drug for various toxicities.
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 668 (Book Page): "Reversible infertility occurs in men, but sulfasalazine does not affect fertility in women. The drug does not appear to be teratogenic."

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What common adverse effects are associated with low-dose Methotrexate in RA?
back:
- Nausea and mucosal ulcers
- Leukopenia and anemia
- Dose-related hepatotoxicity (enzyme elevation)
- Hypersensitivity-like lung reactions
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 652 (Book Page): [Nausea and mucosal ulcers are the most common toxicities. Additionally, many other side effects such as leukopenia, anemia, stomatitis, GI ulcerations, and alopecia are probably the result of inhibiting cellular proliferation.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What is the mechanism of NSAID-induced nephrotoxicity in RA patients?
back:
- Interference with renal blood flow autoregulation
- Modulated by prostaglandin inhibition
- Leads to fluid retention and hyperkalemia
- Risk of renal papillary necrosis
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 644 (Book Page): [Nephrotoxicity, reported for all NSAIDs, is due, in part, to interference with the autoregulation of renal blood flow, which is modulated by prostaglandins.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Compare the monitoring requirements for Hydroxychloroquine versus Sulfasalazine.
back:
- Hydroxychloroquine: Ophthalmologic examination every 12 months (retinal toxicity)
- Sulfasalazine: Complete blood count (CBC) for neutropenia (1–5% occurrence)
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 650 (Book Page): [ophthalmologic monitoring every 12 months is advised]; Page 653 (Book Page): [Neutropenia occurs in 1–5% of patients]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Why must patients be screened for latent tuberculosis before starting TNF-alpha blockers?
back:
- TNF-alpha is vital for macrophage-dependent granuloma maintenance
- Inhibition increases risk of latent TB reactivation
- Risk is relatively lower with Etanercept than other blockers
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 655 (Book Page): [The risk of bacterial infections and macrophage-dependent infection (including tuberculosis... is increased... Activation of latent tuberculosis is lower with etanercept than with other TNF-alpha–blocking agents.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Which metabolic and laboratory parameters require monitoring during Tocilizumab therapy?
back:
- Fasting lipid profile (cholesterol, triglycerides, LDL, HDL)
- Liver enzymes (ALT/AST)
- Platelet count and Neutrophils
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): [The most common adverse reactions are... elevated liver enzymes. Neutropenia and reduction in platelet counts occur occasionally, and lipids (eg, cholesterol, triglycerides, LDL, and HDL) should be monitored.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What is the primary absolute contraindication for the use of Leflunomide in RA?
back:
- Pregnancy (proven teratogenic risk)
- Severe hepatic impairment
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 651 (Book Page): [Elevation in liver enzymes can occur... This drug is contraindicated in pregnancy.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: How does the concomitant use of Ibuprofen affect patients on Aspirin for cardioprotection?
back:
- Ibuprofen antagonizes irreversible platelet inhibition by Aspirin
- Limits Aspirin's cardioprotective effects
- May decrease total anti-inflammatory effectiveness
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 648 (Book Page): [The concomitant administration of ibuprofen and aspirin antagonizes the irreversible platelet inhibition induced by aspirin... may limit the cardioprotective effects of aspirin.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: A patient on high-dose Glucocorticoids for RA requires surgery. What precaution is necessary?
back:
- Supplementary "stress doses" of corticosteroids
- Compensates for suppressed hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis
- Prevents acute adrenal crisis
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 713 (Book Page): [Even patients maintained on relatively low doses of corticosteroids may require supplementary therapy at times of stress, such as when surgical procedures are performed]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: What are the characteristic adverse effects of Tofacitinib on lipid profiles?
back:
- Dose-dependent increase in LDL (Low-Density Lipoprotein)
- Increase in HDL (High-Density Lipoprotein)
- Increase in total cholesterol
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 657 (Book Page): [Dose-dependent increases in the levels of low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and total cholesterol have been found in patients receiving tofacitinib.]

category: Identify important adverse effects, major toxicities, precautions, and contraindications of RA drugs
front: Q: Describe the effect of Sulfasalazine on male versus female fertility.
back:
- Men: Reversible infertility (reduced sperm count/motility)
- Women: No significant effect on fertility
citation: In book "Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology", Page 653 (Book Page): [Reversible infertility occurs in men, but sulfasalazine does not affect fertility in women.]
